# RFC-014: Migrate auth from session cookies to JWT

**Author:** Priya S.  
**Status:** Draft  
**Target release:** 2026Q3

## Background

Our web app currently authenticates users with opaque session cookies backed by a Redis store. We have one Redis cluster per region and the session lookup adds ~3ms p50, ~18ms p99 to every authenticated request. The mobile team is also building a new native app and they have asked for a token-based scheme so they can avoid the cookie jar work on iOS.

This RFC proposes replacing session cookies with JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for both web and mobile clients.

## Goals

- Remove the per-request Redis lookup from the hot path.
- Give mobile a token that travels in an `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- Ship behind a feature flag in Q3.

## Non-goals

- OAuth flows. We are not adding third-party auth in this RFC.
- Refresh-token rotation. Out of scope for v1; can be added later.

## Proposal

### Token format

We will issue JWTs signed with HS256 using a shared secret. Payload:

```
{
  "sub": "<user_id>",
  "iat": <unix>,
  "exp": <unix + 7 days>,
  "role": "admin" | "member" | "viewer"
}
```

The shared secret will live in our existing secrets manager and be loaded into every backend service at boot.

### Issuance

The `/login` endpoint will return the JWT in the response body. The web client stores it in `localStorage`; the mobile client stores it in its own secure storage. The cookie path is removed entirely.

### Verification

Each backend service verifies the JWT locally on every request. No Redis call. Expired tokens (>7 days) return 401 and the client re-logs in.

### Revocation

For v1, we accept that we cannot revoke a token before its `exp`. Compromised tokens will simply expire within 7 days. If we need to invalidate a session sooner (e.g. password change), we will rotate the shared HS256 secret, which will invalidate every JWT in flight.

### Migration

We will ship a feature flag `auth_jwt_enabled`. When on for a user, `/login` returns a JWT and the cookie is cleared. When off, the existing cookie flow runs unchanged. We will flip the flag at 10% / 50% / 100% on consecutive days.

## Open questions

- Should we use RS256 instead of HS256? Probably not — HS256 is simpler.
- Should we cap the token at 24h instead of 7 days? TBD.

## Rollout

1. Ship code behind the flag.
2. Flip to 10% on Tuesday, 50% on Wednesday, 100% on Thursday.
3. Delete the session-cookie path two weeks after 100%.
